facts.statement: Fossils of Hamadasuchus have been found in the Kem Kem Formation in southeastern Morocco.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from the Kem Kem Formation outcropping in southeastern Morocco.

facts.statement: Hamadasuchus lived during the Albian and Cenomanian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: These beds date back to the Albian and Cenomanian stages of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Hamadasuchus was originally classified in the family Trematochampsidae.
facts.quote: It was first assigned to the family Trematochampsidae.

facts.statement: Hamadasuchus is characterized by lateromedially compressed and serrated teeth.
facts.quote: Diagnostic features of the genus include its lateromedially compressed and serrated teeth.

facts.statement: Hamadasuchus had a deep snout and a slightly heterodont dentition featuring three distinct tooth morphologies in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: It was deep-snouted and had a slightly heterodont dentition with three distinct tooth morphologies present from sections of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: Hamadasuchus belongs to the family Peirosauridae.
The genus Hamadasuchus was described by Buffetaut in 1994.
Hamadasuchus lived between 106.3 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Cenomanian (106.3 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species of Hamadasuchus is H. rebouli, while H. taouzensis is a proposed species described by Nicholl et al. in 2021.
facts.quote: subdivision: H. rebouli Buffetaut, 1994 (type) H. taouzensis? Nicholl et al., 2021

facts.statement: Nicholl et al. in 2021 suggested that Antaeusuchus might be a synonym of Hamadasuchus.

rejected.statement: Hamadasuchus is an extinct genus of sebecian crocodylomorph.
rejected.quote: Hamadasuchus is an extinct genus of sebecian crocodylomorph.
